answer: A staking-and-slash reef of bonded deposits makes sybil identity expensive. Each agent locks collateral its peers can slash if it spawns fake identities: ten sock-puppets cost ten bonds, turning free clones into a funded attack. Endless free agents are just plume decoration, not real capacity. The fable that verified identity alone stops sybils fails because fake credentials are cheap; only an economic reef of deposits, slashing, and attested stake histories raises the cost per identity so attackers must spend as much as honest agents to matter.
